claims.claim: Reviewers state that a large portion of the game's content, maps, vehicles, and weapons are locked behind downloadable content (DLC).

citations.review_text: The game is alright buy why the hell does almost everything require a damn dlc?!

This game is garbage compared to The Hunter: Classic. Just an arcade style DLC hell. Graphics aren't everything in a hunting game. I spent  thousands of hours and years of my life on Classic. COTW simply does not compare.

Loaded in and was immediately amazed by the ambience. Shot a deer tracked it, found it, and got paid. Next session shot a bear tracked it for about 45 minutes of game time never found it. Got rushed by a moose. Put a tree between me and it then proceeded to plug it with 12 well placed shots from my .357 -- no impact. Got knocked out. 

No longer want to play a walking simulator with invincible moose that have their way with you. I've got to add if you don't have any DLC content your missing half the game as well, which feels... dirty.
I didn't like it because it was too slow for me. Its a fine game don't get me wrong, but the majority of the game is DLC's.

I get why someone would like it, but I found it pretty boring. I also don't like that there are 2 DLCs that should be included in the main game as well as plenty of DLCs that feel like nickel and diming you. I can't imagine how frustrating it would be to have bought this game at full price just to keep getting locked out of content.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay loop as very slow-paced, involving extensive periods of walking, tracking animals for long durations, and struggling to find targets.

citations.review_text: takes hours to find a deer

I came here to hunt... and somehow ended up relaxing for hours.

At first, I thought theHunter: Call of the Wild would just be another hunting game. I couldn't have been more wrong.

This game is one of the most beautiful and immersive experiences I've played. The environments are stunning, the wildlife feels alive, and every hunt tells its own story. Sometimes you'll spend 20 minutes tracking a single animal, and when you finally get the perfect shot, it feels incredibly rewarding.

What I love most is that the game lets you play at your own pace. You don't have to rush or constantly be in action. You can explore massive maps, enjoy the scenery, listen to nature, and hunt whenever you're ready. It's surprisingly relaxing after a long day.

Why you should play it:

🌲 Beautiful open-world maps with incredible attention to detail.
🦌 Realistic animal behavior that makes every hunt unique.
🎯 Rewarding gameplay where patience and skill pay off.
🤝 Great solo or with friends.
🎧 Amazing sound design that makes the world feel alive.

Even if you've never been interested in hunting, this game is worth trying. It's just as much about exploring nature and enjoying the journey as it is about taking the shot.

If you're looking for a game that's both relaxing and rewarding, theHunter: Call of the Wild is an easy recommendation.

10/10 – The only game where walking for 30 minutes without seeing anything somehow turns into one of the best gaming sessions you've had.

got it for 2-3$ cant lie its not worth more than that.. super slow paced range usually doesnt go above 20-30m and you have to crouch walk everything because animals can hear you from 150m away so it takes about 40min just to have a shot on a buck, and the bullet is so weak that you will probably have to shoot it 1-2times more than that.

Very disappointing. Read most of the so called positive reviews but cannot understand  exactly how this game actually warrants them. Wander around aimlessly, tracking animals that seem to wander off in all directions. Graphics are good yes, but pointless if you just spend ages just wandering about.
Overall not recommended and just glad it wasn't very much money to be wasted .

You will love it if: You enjoy immersive, beautiful open worlds, appreciate realistic ballistics, and find a slow-paced gameplay loop rewarding. It is a fantastic game to put on headphones, relax, or listen to a podcast to while tracking game.

You should skip it if: You are looking for fast-paced action, instant gratification, or direct mission structures. If you don't possess a high tolerance for tracking a single prize elk through a forest for 30 minutes, it will feel like a tedious "walking simulator."

I remember the days when a hunting simulator was a very self contained package and dlc was meant to expand and keep it interesting. What we have here is a base level game that feels more like an extended demo and the ever increasing dlc adding what should have been standard features to the game. You do get a "full" game if you purchase the base game. It has two maps standard, no vehicles, no dogs, very limited selection of weapons and animals. Missions are stupid and often really dull.

The graphices are pretty average and even at native resolution with antialiasing set high it looks really fuzzy. Colour pallettes are plain and don't change much with the day and seasons. Aniaml patterns of behaviour are really obvious and repeat meaning there is very little stalking required an mostly just patient waiting.

Pretty shallow gun physics and a hard to access shooting range make this game one of my least favourite hunting sims ever

[h1]Give us the ATV.[/h1]
I wanted an authentic and immersive hunting experience, and that’s what I got. This game looks stunning, sounds incredible, and runs smoothly. Beyond its simple controls and accommodating settings, the attention to detail and level of realism are equally impressive. 
Unfortunately, the heavy reliance on DLC makes for a VERY boring experience if you don't feel like paying extra. I understand cosmetics, but an ATV? Every outpost is damn near a mile apart, and they couldn’t include the four-wheeler in the base game? Not to mention the dozen or so weapon packs. CotW has been out for nearly a decade, but the great majority of its content is locked behind paywalls.

citations.review_text: the game is beautiful, the nature is stunning and I absolutely love it. I've played it for hundreds of hours and it doesn't get boring. the only thing that i hate about it is the fact that there are so many DLCs and without them your options are pretty limited but with them the game is 10x more enjoyable.

A little arcadey for realistic shooting but it still offers great gameplay for what it offers.

It's rather insane with the DLC's and i wouldn't have minded if it was just cosmetic stuff and maps but, some of them include Guns which you can only get if you buy the entire map DLC. If you want the .303 British for instance than tough as you need to buy the DLC map that it comes bundled with to gain access to it, even if you don't want/care to play that particular map. You're basically paying full DLC price for 1 gun. (This is more than likely why everyone says to ONLY buy DLC's when they are on sale .... *Sigh)

The game itself though is fun and engaging, and you can lose yourself for hours if this is the sort of stuff you like to play so i'll happily give it a recommendation.

theHunter: Call of the Wild is a fantastic game if you just want to sit back and enjoy the experience. Unlike most modern games, it doesn't force a fast pace or stressful grind on you. You can easily boot it up for just an hour to enjoy the beautiful scenery, walk around, and hunt at your own leisure.
However, the entry barrier can be quite high. To fully enjoy the game, you almost need the DLCs, and buying them at full price adds up quickly. I highly recommend waiting for a sale. The base game often drops to around $2–$5, and the DLCs get heavily discounted as well. (If you don't want to wait for a Steam sale, look for key sellers online - it is way less expensive)

The best hunting simulator out there, but it has one major problem: the overwhelming number of DLCs that make the game easier or simply more enjoyable. If you want the full experience, you'll end up spending 60€ or more, as the developers seem to keep "solving problems" by releasing new DLCs—better weapons, new maps, dogs, scopes, tents, vehicles, feeders, electronic callers, and much more. Good luck enjoying the game without all of that.

I’ve been playing this game for 7.5 years, and I can confirm that if you’re not a fan of grinding and extensive progression systems. This game will likely not be for you unless you really appreciate hunting. It is also has somewhat of an arcade feel. I wouldn’t neccesarily call it “unrealistic”. However, if you get better at the game, you can get a lot done in 1-3 hours. The introduction of Great One species which are incredibly rare, has added a lot of “grinding” for players, which can definitely draw people away from the game. This game also takes a long time to progress. It took me almost a whole year to get to the maximum level of 60. And I played for over 300 hours in that year. Across all platforms, multiple lost steam accounts, I have spent well over 7,000 hours in the game. Starting up a new save file can and will always feel slow. And you don’t get access to a lot of the weapons quickly, unless you pay extra for the DLC. Speaking of dlcs, the game is $20, there are several dlcs that add new firearms, which are free to buy in game. Most of those dlcs are around $4. The game is very reliant on paid dlcs, at least if you want to experience everything. There are 18+ reserves, the base game gives you access to just 2. And a very minimal amount of weapons. I suppose you could get away with the base game, but it’s incredibly unideal. The game is well over 100gb, and you need quite a beefy pc to run high graphics. For reference, my PC, can run Far Cry Primal on high perfectly, running this game on Low graphics, gives me about 45-50fps. So be aware of that. The game is super fun, and there’s a reason i’ve played it for so long, but it’s very unbeginner friendly. You will likely have to be very dedicated, and or appreciative of hunting as a whole to progress in this game. claims.claim: Reviewers report that successful hunting requires managing mechanics such as wind direction, noise, scent, animal daily behaviors, and anatomical shot placement.

citations.review_text: This game sharpens my thinking.  There are so many considerations including map mastery, game locations, time of day, wind, visibility, noise, weapon and ammo selection, heart rate, etc., etc.

It's a game that offers a very high level of mental challenge. Players don't just walk around, find an animal, and shoot it. They have to pay attention to the wind direction so their scent doesn't drift toward the target, control the noise they make depending on the type of ground they're walking on, and learn the animals' daily behavior, such as when they drink, feed, or rest.

On top of that, players need to understand the anatomy of each species, knowing where vital organs like the lungs, heart, liver, and spine are located to make an effective shot. Finally, hunting top-tier animals like a "Great One" or a "Diamond" requires careful population management across the map, strategic planning, and a bit of luck.

theHunter: Call of the Wild is a relaxing and immersive hunting game with beautiful environments and realistic wildlife behavior. It rewards patience and careful planning, making every successful hunt feel satisfying. If you enjoy exploring nature and taking your time, it's definitely worth playing.
